successors.description: Wire 5.5 From one version to the next, spec 8.3: a reader holds held, written at service time held_time, and reads newer, written at newer_time, which no longer lists a held entry. newer counts that entry in its totals, as a compaction writes it. The reader accepts newer when the entry's at + longest period + 60 s was before some service time from held_time to newer_time, the longest period taken at that time, so an anchored month or year limit's entry compacted in a shorter period is accepted in a version written in a longer one. A held_time after newer_time judges at newer_time alone. accepted is the verdict.

description: Allowance usage (wire 5.5, spec 8.3 with specs/allowances.md): for every period limit the amount and count of counted entries in the period containing t (anchored) or with t < at + 60 s + L (rolling), the lifetime amount including compacted totals, and entry counts reserved, spent and released. A ledger or claim done, or a validated payer proof, spends. Open and unknown claims reserve entries without an outcome. Every failed attempt is released, whoever wrote the failure, while its claim remains and after it is gone: it counts in no amount and no count. Done or a paid proof overrides the release and spends. An entry without an outcome whose claim is gone spends. Compacted totals.failed items use the same rule for lifetime usage. Candidates are checked against every limit; refused_by names the first limit that refuses. failure_evidence holds pure counting inputs: evidence means already validated payer-proof evidence (paid), not a shared record member, and the failure itself comes from the claim, the entry or the compacted item; Callers must bind it to the attempt, obligation, Allowance, amount, asset and owner. Its compacted cases replace the entry with one totals.failed item. period_limit_spellings checks duplicate terms by wire spelling; period_limit_members checks required members. compaction/successors checks which newer ledger versions a reader holding an older one accepts after a compaction it didn't see.

A period limit carries both, each possibly null, not both null; a missing one isn't read as null, so every reader refuses these terms. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

period_limit_spellings.description: Wire 4.15, specs/allowances.md: the terms of the first case with period_limits replaced. Two period limits are duplicates when every member is equal as spelled on the wire: amount_limit and anchor compare as strings, so numerically equal amounts (1, 1.0) or one instant spelled two ways are distinct entries; payment_count_limit and every compare as integers; kind and unit exactly. accepted are terms every reader takes, with each of their period limits; refused are terms with an entry twice, which every reader refuses. reason is paykit-lib's wording.
